segments.t: What changed in the current release. The version this guide was built for is shown in the footer.

KTPH000New layoutKTPH001 — the Connection Manager shows a library on the left (all connections, favorites, recently used, open now, folders, tags, teamwork), the chosen connections in the middle and an inspector on the right, with every detail of the selected connection and quick edits of its name and tag. The toolbar uses icons in the style of the icon toolbar, and the list shows each connection's address, tag and marks for jump server, tunnels, isolation and incognito instead of emoji. See KTPH002Connection ManagerKTPH003.

KTPH000MapKTPH001 — KTPH002MapKTPH003 shows the connections as a network plan: a zone per folder in its tab color, jump-server routes and tunnels as lines, double-click connects and dragging a node into another zone moves the connection into that folder. See KTPH004List and mapKTPH005.
KTPH000FavoritesKTPH001 — mark connections with the star to find them under KTPH002FavoritesKTPH003; teamwork connections can be favorites too.
KTPH000Teamwork beside local connectionsKTPH001 — the general lists show teamwork connections too, marked with a small people symbol and read-only. See KTPH002LibraryKTPH003.

KTPH000OS symbolsKTPH001 — give each server the symbol of its operating system (Windows, macOS, Linux distributions, ChromeOS, Unix, BSD, z/OS) or one of your own images, shown in the list, on the map and in the inspector. See KTPH002OS symbolsKTPH003.
KTPH000Map as PDFKTPH001 — KTPH002PDFKTPH003 on the map saves it as a vector PDF with the korTTY logo, in landscape or portrait.

KTPH000Overview exportKTPH001 — KTPH002Export overviewKTPH003 writes your servers as JSON, YAML, TOML or XML, with the parts you choose and never a password or key. See KTPH004Exporting an overviewKTPH005.
KTPH000InspectorKTPH001 — the route from this computer through the jump server, security as chips, usage bars for the last 14 days and an SFTP button.

KTPH000Serial portsKTPH001 — the new KTPH002SerialKTPH003 protocol opens a terminal on a serial port, like PuTTY's serial sessions: a router or switch console, a microcontroller board or a USB-to-serial adapter, on Windows, macOS and Linux. Pick the port from the list or type it, and set the speed, data bits, parity, stop bits, flow control, what Enter sends, DTR/RTS and local echo. KTPH004Send BreakKTPH005 is in the terminal's context menu and in the Connections menu, and can get a key in the keyboard settings. Serial sessions from MobaXterm and PuTTY Connection Manager files are imported too. See KTPH006Serial connectionsKTPH007.

KTPH000PowerShell and Command Prompt in the toolbarKTPH001 — on Windows, the Terminal group of the icon toolbar gets KTPH002New PowerShellKTPH003 and KTPH004New Command PromptKTPH005 right after KTPH006New local shellKTPH007, each with its own icon; saved layouts gain both once. With Git for Windows installed, the customization catalog also offers KTPH008New Git BashKTPH009. See KTPH010Customizing the icon toolbarKTPH011.

KTPH000Local shells run under ConPTYKTPH001 — local shells and the native Mosh client now start under the Windows pseudo console instead of winpty, which no longer interferes with keys typed into other applications while korTTY runs.
KTPH002Mosh Client finds mosh-client.exeKTPH003 — the Mosh Client (native) protocol now looks for KTPH000 in the folders of the KTPH001. See KTPH004ProtocolsKTPH005.

KTPH000Toolbar groups wrap instead of shrinkingKTPH001 — when the window is too narrow, whole toolbar groups move to another line, so every button stays directly clickable instead of hiding behind an overflow chevron. See KTPH002Customizing the icon toolbarKTPH003.

KTPH000Focus ring can be switched offKTPH001 — switch off KTPH002Frame the split pane the keyboard is inKTPH003 in the Window settings to hide the ring around the active split pane. You then recognize the active pane by its cursor. See KTPH004TabsKTPH005.

KTPH000Folder analysis by fileKTPH001 — the folder analysis tab lists the folder's files beside the report. Pick a file, or step through the files with ◀ ▶ and the arrow keys, to see only its findings and a short description of what the file does; each row shows how many of its findings are ticked, and its checkbox ticks or clears them all. Findings keep their file even when the model numbers them per file or names the file another way. See KTPH002Analysing a folder as one projectKTPH003.

KTPH000Vertical or horizontal flow diagramKTPH001 — an KTPH002OrientationKTPH003 control in the diagram toolbar draws the flowchart top to bottom or left to right, in the analysis panel, its zoom window and the Diagram dialog. Switching redraws the stored diagram without asking the AI again. See KTPH004Diagram appearanceKTPH005.

KTPH000"Model default" instead of "Disabled"KTPH001 — the reasoning setting that sends no reasoning parameter is now called KTPH002Model defaultKTPH003, because the model's own default then applies; only KTPH004NoneKTPH005 switches reasoning off. A tooltip on the dropdown explains the difference. See KTPH006Reasoning Effort LevelsKTPH007.

KTPH000Connection test accepts reasoning-only repliesKTPH001 — KTPH002Test AI ConnectionKTPH003 and KTPH004Refresh reasoning optionsKTPH005 now pass when a model that reasons by default, such as Qwen in LM Studio, spends the short test reply on reasoning, and a failed refresh names the endpoint's own reason.
KTPH000Dismissed sessions stay dismissedKTPH001 — closing the last tab on purpose now empties the session snapshot, so the restore offer no longer comes back at every start after you discard it.
KTPH000Steady diagram tooltipsKTPH001 — the code-reference tooltip in the enlarged analysis diagram stays open while the mouse rests on a node instead of flashing and closing.
KTPH000Folder analyses survive a malformed keyKTPH001 — an analysis whose JSON lacks the opening quote of one key is repaired instead of being discarded as "no usable analysis".
KTPH000German label for reasoningKTPH001 — the German user interface now labels this setting of AI profiles "Reasoning", as the guide does.

KTPH000Wide dialogs open at their size in the AtlantaFX designsKTPH001 — under an AtlantaFX design, a dialog laid out wider than 600 px (such as the settings, KTPH002Compare foldersKTPH003 in the SFTP manager or the KTPH004Logfile ManagerKTPH005) opened squeezed or grew after it appeared; it now opens as wide as in the Normal design, and a long message still wraps.
